about: Nuke's on-screen Viewer controls for 2D nodes, one entry per control, from Foundry's Nuke 17.0 Reference Guide node pages and the User Guide's Transforming in 2D page. Facts only: a control or a rule the pages read do not state is listed with status 'undocumented' and no claim; a node Nuke gives no on-screen control is listed under 'no_controls'. tools/nuke_viewer_controls.py drives NodeBased's viewer handles against every documented entry (lane 10, step T3, 2026-11-17). Roto and RotoPaint are measured row by row in docs/ROTO_NUKE_UI.md and are left out here.

rg_pages.title: Radial, Ramp, Rectangle, Position, Reformat, Flare, Blur and Defocus (Nuke 17.0 Reference Guide node pages)

controls.nuke: Drag the centre of the transform jack to translate: translate x and y follow the pointer.
controls.quote: C) Drag to translate the frame

controls.nuke: Shift+drag the centre constrains the translation to x or y.
controls.quote: Shift+drag to constrain the translation to x or y.

controls.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+drag the centre repositions the pivot point (center x, y).
controls.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+drag to reposition the pivot point (the point that acts as the center to transformation operations).

controls.nuke: Drag the circle of the jack to scale on x and y together.
controls.quote: B) Drag to scale the frame uniformly - simultaneously on x and y

controls.nuke: Drag the left or right point on the circle to scale on x only (scale's w).
controls.quote: The top and bottom points scale on y; the left and right points, on x.

controls.nuke: Drag the top or bottom point on the circle to scale on y only (scale's h).
controls.quote: The top and bottom points scale on y; the left and right points, on x.

controls.nuke: Drag the horizontal bar to rotate around the pivot.
controls.quote: E) Drag to rotate the frame around the pivot point

controls.nuke: Rotating snaps to typical values; Shift while dragging turns the snapping off.
controls.quote: The transform overlay snaps to typical values. To prevent the snapping, press Shift while dragging.

controls.nuke: Drag the vertical bar to skew (rotate the pixel columns around the pivot).
controls.quote: Or drag the vertical bar of the transformation overlay.

controls.nuke: With invert checked, a small transform handle appears next to the standard one.
controls.quote: When the box is checked, a small transform handle appears next to the standard transform handle in the Viewer.

controls.nuke: The pages read do not state whether the jack needs the node selected or its panel open.
The pages read do not state whether moving the pivot also changes translate so the picture stays put.
Drag the crop box's edges in the Viewer to move that side of the box.
controls.quote: You can also adjust the crop box in the Viewer by dragging its edges.

controls.nuke: Move and resize the on-screen text box in the Viewer; the text wraps inside it.
controls.quote: You can also move and resize the box in the Viewer. Your text is wrapped inside the box you defined.

controls.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+drag moves the center of rotation and scaling.
controls.quote: Sets the center of rotation and scaling. You can also move it using Ctrl/Cmd +drag.

controls.nuke: Drag the ROI's edges in the Viewer to move that side of the region of interest; its default covers the whole of input A.
controls.quote: You can also adjust the ROI in the Viewer by dragging its edges.

controls.nuke: The ROI box can be adjusted with the Viewer connected to input A rather than the ColorTransfer node.
controls.quote: When adjusting the ROI, you may want to connect the Viewer to input A rather than the ColorTransfer node, so you can better see the area you are selecting.

controls.nuke: Each track has an anchor in the Viewer; adding a track places a new anchor there.
controls.quote: Click to add a new track and anchor to the Viewer.

controls.nuke: The source and destination grids show lines and handles in the Viewer, each with its own visible and locked switch.
controls.quote: When enabled, the Destination Grid lines and handles are visible.

controls.nuke: A transformation overlay moves the whole grid; dragging an axis of it scales or rotates.
controls.quote: Alternatively, you can drag on an axis on the transformation overlay in the Viewer.

controls.nuke: The page names the four pins as the image corners but does not describe dragging them in the Viewer. NodeBased draws the four to-pins, which drag (measured by tests/test_l10_t9_point_handles.py).
controls.pages_read: Read 11/19 (lane 10 step T9): the Nuke 17.0 Reference Guide page CornerPin2D and the User Guide page Transforming in 2D; neither describes dragging the pins in the Viewer.

controls.nuke: The page states no on-screen control. NodeBased draws the output box when the type is to box; its edges and corners set width and height, and it has no position to move (measured by tests/test_l10_t9_point_handles.py).
